title: One independent leaf: domain stability and realization square
statement: Fix the coefficient and realization data of [def-pur-realization-tree-shift-data] with $\ell\ne p$. Assume the inverse-unit and unary and tensor-slot insertion laws [def-pur-realization-adjunction-insertion-shift-data] and the actual recursion equations [lem-pur-integral-realization-recursion]. For every finite independent expression $e$, geometric witness, admissible integral input family $K$, label $i$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$, the family $K^{(i,r)}$ is admissible and its specified realization satisfies $c_{e,K^{(i,r)}}\,I_e=S_e\,c_{e,K}[r]$ in diagrammatic order, where $I_e$ and $S_e$ are exactly the designated integralShift and sourceShift. No generator transport or multiple-input assertion is made.

proof.text: Fix a leaf $i$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$, and write $K'$ for the family with only $K_i$ replaced by $K_i[r]$. First check admissibility. Integral constructibility and completeness are preserved by shifts by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. At a system level, shift every strict complex and its transition maps. The normalized transition-adjoint map becomes $\alpha_{m,n}[r]$ under $(M_m[r])\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n\cong(M_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n)[r]$, using the localized cochain tensor shift, so it is still invertible. Shift an etale-origin witness $(L_n,\alpha_n)$ to $(L_n[r],\alpha_n[r])$ with its exact inverse-image comparison; its transition compatibilities are the shifted original equalities. Cohomology satisfies $H^a(M[r])=H^{a+r}(M)$; thus constructibility and common cohomological bounds persist. The Tor-interval shift lemma gives $[a-r,b-r]$ at every level, independently of $n$. Recursively use the operation shift isomorphisms along the unique path from $i$ to the root: each affected intermediate is isomorphic to its old value shifted by $r$, and every other intermediate is unchanged. Include the hidden open intermediate of compact support. There are finitely many intermediates, so the minima and maxima of the old and translated endpoints give common finite intervals. This proves stability of the entire admissible domain without asserting preservation of that domain on arbitrary inputs.

proof.text: Expand each compactSupport constructor into the explicit proper push of the open extension along compactProper and compactOpen. Retain its hidden open intermediate in the admissible domain and the induced geometric witnesses. By induction, supportExpansion and its unary/tensor contexts give the canonical pair to the expanded tree. Both interpreted maps are identity, by the recorded composite definitions. Realizations.coherence identifies the actual comparison components along this pair. The selected shift isomorphisms agree by the fixed composite CommShift formula and functoriality. The expanded expression is BasicTree, so the assumed recursion now applies at every vertex. No recursion equation is invoked on a compactSupport constructor itself.

proof.text: Put $M_X=X(\mathcal RK)$ and $D_X=X_{\rm int}(K)$. For each subtree containing $i$, denote its recursively specified system comparison by $s_X:M_X'\to M_X[r]$, put $S_X=\chi_{\mathcal L}\mathcal L(s_X)$, and denote its integral comparison by $I_X:D_X'\to D_X[r]$. Prove $I_Xc_X'=c_X[r]S_X$ by structural induction on that subtree. The occurrence definition gives exactly one child containing $i$ at every vertex; at tensor vertices the other child is fixed. At the leaf, $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$ by the actual recursion, so the desired equality is exactly the assumed inverse-unit shift square. These comparisons and this base square are natural in the whole input family.

proof.text:
For a unary vertex $AX$, write $a=a_A(M_X)$ and $a'=a_A(M_X')$. The recursively defined shift is $I_{AX}=\chi_{A_{\rm int}}A_{\rm int}(I_X)$. Expand the actual recursion and calculate, with each $\chi$ evaluated at the displayed operands:
$$\begin{aligned}
 I_{AX}c_{AX}'&=\chi_{A_{\rm int}}A_{\rm int}(I_Xc_X')a'\\
 &=\chi_{A_{\rm int}}A_{\rm int}(c_X[r]S_X)a'\\
 &=A_{\rm int}(c_X)[r]\,\chi_{A_{\rm int}}A_{\rm int}(S_X)a'\\
 &=A_{\rm int}(c_X)[r]a[r]S_{AX}=c_{AX}[r]S_{AX}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is the child induction hypothesis; the third is naturality of the operation shift; the fourth is precisely the assumed shift square for $a_A$, precomposed with the system child comparison. Functoriality justifies each expansion. Compact support is the specified composite of its open and proper vertices.

proof.text:
At a tensor vertex $X\otimes Y$ suppose first that $i\in\operatorname{Occ}(X)$. Put $a=a_\otimes(M_X,M_Y)$, $a'=a_\otimes(M_X',M_Y)$, and write $\boxtimes$ for completed integral tensor. With $\chi_1$ the first-slot comparison, the same explicit calculation is
$$\begin{aligned}
 I_{X\otimes Y}c_{X\otimes Y}'
 &=\chi_1((I_Xc_X')\boxtimes c_Y)a'\\
 &=\chi_1((c_X[r]S_X)\boxtimes c_Y)a'\\
 &=(c_X\boxtimes c_Y)[r]\,\chi_1(S_X\boxtimes1)a'\\
 &=(c_X\boxtimes c_Y)[r]a[r]S_{X\otimes Y}.
\end{aligned}$$
Use child induction, naturality of $\chi_1$, and the assumed first-slot square of $a_\otimes$ in that order. If $i\in\operatorname{Occ}(Y)$ instead, the lines are $\chi_2(c_X\boxtimes(I_Yc_Y'))a'$, then $\chi_2(c_X\boxtimes(c_Y[r]S_Y))a'$, then $(c_X\boxtimes c_Y)[r]\chi_2(1\boxtimes S_Y)a'$, and finally $(c_X\boxtimes c_Y)[r]a[r]S_{X\otimes Y}$, with $a'=a_\otimes(M_X,M_Y')$. Here $\chi_2$ is exactly the signed second-slot comparison, with coefficient $(-1)^{rj}$ on first degree $j$; its naturality and assumed insertion square use that same comparison throughout. No symmetry or exchange of slots is used. The recursion identifies the final line with $c_{X\otimes Y}[r]S_{X\otimes Y}$. This completes the finite-tree induction, naturally in every input.

theorem realizationTreeSingleShift (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (o : Operations l E) (R : Realizations l E D o)
    (_hInsertion : RealizationAdjunctionInsertionShift l E D o R)
    (_hRecursion : ∀ {I : Type u} [Finite I]
      {X : I → Over (Spec (.of D.k))} {W : Over (Spec (.of D.k))}
      (e : Expression _ I X W) (ge : e.geometric) (K : (e.domain l E o).FullSubcategory),
      Recursion.BasicTree e → Recursion.Equations l E R R.comparison e ge K)
    : (∀ {I : Type u} [Finite I] {X : I → Over (Spec (.of D.k))}
      {W : Over (Spec (.of D.k))} (e : IndependentExpression _ I X W)
      (ge : e.val.geometric) (K : (e.val.domain l E o).FullSubcategory) (i : I) (r : ℤ),
      ∃ h : e.val.domain l E o (Function.update K.obj i ((K.obj i)⟦r⟧)),
        (R.comparison e.val ge).hom.app ⟨Function.update K.obj i ((K.obj i)⟦r⟧), h⟩ ≫
            (e.integralShift l E K.obj i r).hom =
          (e.sourceShift l E o K.obj i r).hom ≫
            ((R.comparison e.val ge).hom.app K)⟦r⟧')
